articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the August 1995 issue (Volume 6, Number 8) of "SJAA EPHEMERIS," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: The article reports on the July General Meeting of the San Jose Astronomical Association, featuring famed comet hunter Don Machholz, who discussed his experiences, observatory, and Messier Marathons. It also provides a detailed calendar of upcoming events for August and September, including star parties, observational classes, and general meetings. The next meeting will feature Bob Ashford discussing "Project Astro," an initiative connecting amateur astronomers with teachers.

articles.title: Forty Years Ago this month
articles.summary: This article, titled "Forty Years Ago this month," recounts an August meeting where an astronomy club's Articles of Incorporation were read to members, signaling the next step for submission to the California Secretary of State. Members extended a vote of thanks to Mr. Hill for his assistance in the club's incorporation. The meeting took place at San Jose State College and listed the club's officers, including President Bob Brauer and Secretary Jim Van Nuland.

articles.title: Stars Over Silver City and Mt. Graham
articles.summary: The author recounts a trip to Silver City, New Mexico, highlighting the Bear Mountain Guest Ranch as a promising dark sky observing location, complete with star parties and local attractions. They also detail a visit to Mt. Graham in Arizona, providing information on its astronomical observatories, accessibility for stargazers, and camping facilities, noting its potential as a future significant astronomical site.

articles.title: Tracking Mir/Atlantis through 12" SC at 100x!
articles.summary: An observer successfully tracked and viewed the Mir space station and Space Shuttle Atlantis (STS-71) in orbit over Boston using a 12-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope at 100x magnification, employing custom-developed satellite tracking software. The detailed observation described visible features of both spacecraft, and the team plans future CCD imaging, analysis of tumbling rocket boosters, and a space beacon experiment. The event, held at the Boston Museum of Science, also had local news and Sky & Telescope's senior editor present.

articles.title: Potluck Picnic & Super Star Party at Fremont Peak State Park
articles.summary: The Fremont Peak Observatory Association (FPOA) and the Astronomical Association of Northern California (AANC) are co-hosting a Potluck Picnic & Super Star Party at Fremont Peak State Park on Saturday, August 19, 1995. Attendees can view through the 30-inch Challenger Telescope, meet other amateur astronomers, and participate in a potluck with an astronomical/gastronomical contest. The event requires a park fee, and an RSVP by August 17 is requested for planning purposes.

articles.title: Forty Years Ago (cont from pg 1)
articles.summary: This article reports on a club meeting featuring presentations on "Amateur Telescope Making" books by Wes Lindsay, the constellation Cassiopeia by Bob Ferguson, and the Foucault Test by Dr. Geisler. An invitation to the Peninsula club's annual Star Party on September 2nd was announced, and the meeting concluded with a warmly received live demonstration of the Foucault test.

articles.title: Paul Barton Resigns from The Board of directors
articles.summary: Paul Barton has resigned from the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board of Directors after years of service, believing a younger, more active member would better serve the association. He is recognized for his significant, often unseen, contributions, especially single-handedly maintaining the club's Telescope Loaner Program through his personal efforts and expenses. Lew Kurtz has been appointed to fill the vacant board seat.

articles.title: A Look Through A 1960s Vega Telescope
articles.summary: The author details a viewing session comparing an 8-inch SCT with a rare, vintage 1960s Vega 6-inch Maksutov/Newtonian telescope. He highly praises the Vega for its superb build quality and exceptional optical performance, delivering detailed and 'creamy' views of Jupiter and the Moon, comparable to fine modern instruments despite its age. The article emphasizes the enduring quality of high-end vintage optics.

articles.title: Directions to Hogue Park
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to Hogue Park, the location for general meetings, observational astronomy classes, and public star parties. It outlines the start times for various events, including Board of Directors meetings, general meetings, classes, and star parties, welcoming both members and non-members to participate and engage in astronomy.

articles.title: NOTICE - NOTICE
articles.summary: The article announces two significant events for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA): a "Founders Dinner" in October at Kim's Table to celebrate its 40th anniversary, inviting early members and all others to attend. Additionally, a commemorative star party is planned around the October Houge Park Public Star Party to honor John Dobson's 80th birthday. The document also includes the SJAA's calendar for General Meetings, Houge Park Star Parties, and Observational Astronomy Classes from August to December 1995.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This document provides an updated status report for a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes, their current users, and due dates. It indicates which telescopes are currently available for borrowing and includes information on a specialized solar telescope. Instructions are also given for members to borrow equipment or join a waitlist.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS provides a free platform for non-commercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products or services, requiring submissions by the 12th of each month for a three-month run. The current ads feature various used astronomical equipment for sale, including telescopes, mounts, and eyepieces, as well as a 'Lost' notice for a deep cycle battery belonging to SJAA.

articles.title: Lunar Phase Date Rise Trans Set
articles.summary: This document presents a tabular schedule of lunar phases for a specific month, detailing the date, rise, transit, and set times for the First Quarter, Full Moon, Last Quarter, and New Moon. It serves as an ephemeris for key lunar events.

articles.title: Nearer Planets
articles.summary: This article provides an astronomical guide detailing the rise, transit, and set times for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn on three specific dates (07, 17, 27). It also includes their average distance from the Sun (in A.U.) and their apparent magnitude. This data serves as a practical resource for observers interested in tracking the visibility of these 'nearer planets'.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V
articles.summary: This document describes the Sun (SOL) as a G2V type star. It presents a table of astronomical ephemeris data, including rise, transit, and set times, along with corresponding declination values, for the Sun at different observation points or dates.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document provides a table detailing astronomical twilight begin and end times for several dates in July, along with their corresponding Julian Dates. This information is essential for astronomers to plan observation sessions, indicating when the sky is dark enough for astronomical viewing.

articles.title: Sidereal Time
articles.summary: This document presents sidereal time data, showing transit right ascension values at local midnight for several dates. It also details key astronomical times for a "Darkest Saturday Night" on August 26, 1995, including sunset, twilight end, moonset, and dawn begin times.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors, detailing their specific positions such as President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and multiple Directors. For each individual, their name and contact phone number are provided, serving as a directory for the organization's leadership.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document provides a contact list for individuals involved in the production of an ephemeris. It lists several "Ephemeris Contributors" with their phone numbers, and also identifies an "EDITOR" with their contact information.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article provides updates on several comets, noting Periodic Comet d'Arrest's southward movement and Periodic Comet Jackson-Neujmin's brightening. It also reports the recovery of two faint comets, P/1995 M1 (Shoemaker-Levy 4) and P/1995 M 2 (Parker-Hartley), by Jim Scotti. Additionally, it discusses Kazimeras Cernis's analysis of comet hunting success rates, revealing a significant difference in average discovery hours between Northern and Southern Hemisphere observers.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for two comets, 6P/d'Arrest and 58P/Jackson-Neujmin, detailing their predicted positions and estimated magnitudes. The tables cover dates from late July to early September, offering Right Ascension, Declination, elongation, and sky magnitude data for each comet. This information is essential for astronomers and observers looking to locate and track these celestial objects.

articles.title: ORBITAL ELEMENTS
articles.summary: This document provides a table of orbital elements for two comets, 6P/d'Arrest and 58P/Jackson-Neujmin, including data such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period. It cites the Minor Planet Center (MPC) as the source for this technical astronomical data.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing various membership options and their respective costs, including general membership, a membership with a Sky & Telescope subscription, and a junior membership. It provides fields for personal information and instructions on how to submit the completed form and payment to the Treasurer.

articles.title: MAKE CHECKS PAYABLE TO "SJAA"
articles.summary: This document outlines membership options (New, Renewal, Junior, Membership Only, Membership/S&T) for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), instructing members to make checks payable to SJAA. It also provides submission guidelines for articles to the monthly 'EPHEMERIS' publication, including deadlines and editor contact information. The document lists the SJAA's mailing address, non-profit status, and a 24-hour information hotline, dated August 1995.
